Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Signatures

Signature database sync

Read the full FortiWeb signature catalog (classes, sub-classes, signatures and descriptions) from one base FortiWeb into SATOM, so signature pages can show names and be searched.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Administrator → Signatures (URL /signatures/)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • What does it do?
  • Requirements
  • Permissions
  • How to use
  • Configuration
  • Example
  • Result
  • Troubleshooting
  • "Select a base FortiWeb device to sync from."
  • "No FortiWeb appliances configured"
  • "Signature sync from failed" — "No signature set found on the device."
  • "Signature sync read 0 signatures from "
  • The signature editor still says "No signature database cached"

What is it?#

The Signatures page builds SATOM's local reference copy of the FortiWeb signature database. Because the same FortiGuard signature package is on every FortiWeb, one reachable unit — the base device — is enough: SATOM reads every category, sub-class and individual signature with its description, read-only, and keeps the result for the whole instance.

Since 3.0 the same page also shows Signature DB freshness per device — how old each FortiWeb's own signature database is, checked daily. See Signature freshness.

What does it do?#

  • Shows the state of the cached database: number of signatures, number of sub-classes, firmware, signature set and when it was synced.
  • Starts a background job that reads the catalog from the chosen base FortiWeb and replaces the cached copy.
  • Notifies you through the job dock and the notification bell when the job finishes.

The cached catalog is what the Web Protection signature policy editor uses for signature names, descriptions, the class filters and the Signature Details search.

Requirements#

  • At least one registered FortiWeb that SATOM can reach.
  • Nothing is written to the device; the read is read-only.

Permissions#

The page and the sync require users.manage — in practice the Administrator profile. The Administrator menu group, which holds the Signatures entry, is not drawn for users without it, and opening /signatures/ directly returns 403 Forbidden.

ℹ️Note

The FortiADC ADOM has its own Signatures entry in its Administrator menu. That page lists the FortiADC Web Attack Signature policies live from the selected FortiADC and is not related to this catalog; see FortiADC.

How to use#

  1. Open Administrator → Signatures in the FortiWeb ADOM.
  2. Check Cached database: a Cached badge with counts, or No signature database yet.
  3. Under Sync from a base device, choose the Base FortiWeb.
  4. Click Sync now. The page returns at once with Signature sync from started — follow it in the job dock (bottom-right). You'll get a notification when it finishes.
  5. Follow the job (Connecting to…, Selecting signature set…, Reading signature database (set …)…, Saving catalog…).
  6. When the notification arrives, reload the page to see the new counts.

Re-run the sync after a firmware upgrade or a signature package update to pick up new signatures.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Base FortiWeb The device the catalog is read from. Listed as name (host:port) Yes fweb-01 (192.0.2.10:443)

Example#

🧪Example — First sync on a new instance

After registering fweb-01, an administrator opens Administrator → Signatures, picks fweb-01 (192.0.2.10:443) and clicks Sync now. A few moments later the bell shows Signature database synced — N signatures, and the signature editor (FortiWeb → Web Protection → Known Attacks → Signatures, then Signature editor) now lists every signature with its description.

Result#

  • A job named Syncing signatures from in Jobs, finishing with N signatures across M sub-classes.
  • A notification: Signature database synced — N signatures on success, Signature sync read 0 signatures from when nothing was read, or Signature sync from failed on error (see Notifications).
  • Audit entries signatures.sync.start and, on success, signatures.sync.
  • The cached catalog is replaced for the whole instance.

Troubleshooting#

"Select a base FortiWeb device to sync from."#

Possible causes — no device was submitted, or the selected one no longer exists or is not a FortiWeb.

Solution — reload the page and pick a device from the list.

"No FortiWeb appliances configured"#

Solution — register a FortiWeb first (Add Appliance, see Appliances).

"Signature sync from failed" — "No signature set found on the device."#

Possible causes — the base device returned no signature set.

Solution — choose another base FortiWeb, or check the device's signature configuration.

Verification — the next sync ends with Signature database synced.

"Signature sync read 0 signatures from "#

Possible causes — the device answered but returned an empty catalog.

Solution — check the base device, or sync from another FortiWeb.

The signature editor still says "No signature database cached"#

Solution — wait for the job to finish (check the job dock), then reload the signature policy page.

Advanced Internals
  • The catalog is stored as a JSON file in SATOM's data directory (data/signatures.json) and shared by every user and device page.
  • The firmware shown is read best-effort from the device status; a failure to read it never blocks the sync and shows as ?.
  • The same refresh is available as the Sync signature database scheduled action (admin), see Scheduled actions. That action does not record the firmware version.
  • The job runs in a background thread; an unreachable base device marks the job as failed and raises an error notification instead of an error page.
